_README: BENCHMARK CONFIG — the file that turns every 'vs target' indicator from decoration into a real comparison.
Deploy to the dashboard site as: /data/benchmarks.json
Every entry has a sourced industry range AND an hdi_target field.
hdi_target is null until Rob approves it. Until then the dashboard shows the
industry range as REFERENCE, not as a bar HDI is held to. That distinction matters:
an unapproved benchmark is context, an approved one is accountability.
Ranges below are from 2026 sources. Do NOT substitute the widely-circulated
'IT & Services $369.88 / Healthcare $285.82' figures — those come from a 2017
survey that is still republished as current without disclosure.

marketing_sourced_pipeline_pct.label: Marketing-sourced share of pipeline
marketing_sourced_pipeline_pct.hdi_current_note: Not measurable — zero deals carry a campaign association
marketing_sourced_pipeline_pct.interpretation: Below 30% is treated as structural, not an execution issue. HDI cannot compute this at all, which is a more basic problem than underperforming it.
marketing_sourced_pipeline_pct.priority: This is the single benchmark to put in front of Rob.

cost_per_lead_usd.label: Cost per qualified lead
cost_per_lead_usd.hdi_current_note: Not computable — budget on only 5 of 10 conference campaigns, and no agreed lead definition
cost_per_lead_usd.source: 2026 CPL benchmarks — Healthcare IT / Cybersecurity / Insurance Tech band sits above $250; qualified B2B leads $150–$500 generally
cost_per_lead_usd.interpretation: Healthcare IT is one of the most expensive verticals. Benchmark only against your own industry and deal-size cell — CPL spans 24x across industries.

cost_per_lead_tradeshow_usd.label: Cost per lead — trade shows and conferences
cost_per_lead_tradeshow_usd.hdi_current_note: $103,679 tracked spend / 386 influenced contacts. NOT like-for-like: influenced is far looser than a qualified lead. Needs a lead definition before this comparison is honest.
cost_per_lead_tradeshow_usd.source: 2026 SaaS channel CPL benchmarks — trade shows highest CPL of any channel
cost_per_lead_tradeshow_usd.interpretation: Relevant because HDI's entire campaign scope is 10 conferences. On the loosest measure HDI looks well under benchmark, but the measures are not comparable yet.

website_visitor_to_lead_pct.label: Visitor to lead conversion
website_visitor_to_lead_pct.hdi_current_note: Blocked — GA4 is in stub mode, so there is no session denominator
website_visitor_to_lead_pct.source: 2026 B2B funnel conversion benchmarks — healthcare clusters 3–5%, enterprise software 1–3%
website_visitor_to_lead_pct.interpretation: Which band applies depends on whether HDI's motion reads as healthcare services or enterprise software. Worth deciding deliberately rather than picking the flattering one.

mql_to_sql_pct.label: MQL to SQL conversion
mql_to_sql_pct.hdi_current_note: No MQL stage defined in the CRM
mql_to_sql_pct.source: 2026 funnel benchmarks — healthcare and biotech typically exceed 40%
mql_to_sql_pct.interpretation: Healthcare qualifies well because needs are urgent and specific. Under 10% would be structural. HDI has no MQL definition, so this is unmeasured rather than poor.

lead_to_close_pct.label: Lead to closed-won
lead_to_close_pct.source: 2026 B2B SaaS funnel cascade: 1,000 leads to ~390 MQL to ~148 SQL to ~62 opportunities to ~23 closed
lead_to_close_pct.interpretation: Sounds low until weighted by ACV. Useful for volume planning, not for judging quality.

win_rate_by_value_pct.label: Win rate by value
win_rate_by_value_pct.hdi_current_note: $1,178,260 won / $3,180,676 won+lost, from 9 closed deals. Small sample — quote the denominator.
win_rate_by_value_pct.source: 2026 benchmarks — IT and managed services SQL-to-closed around 46%
win_rate_by_value_pct.interpretation: Slightly below the reference band, on a sample too small to call a trend. Suppress this comparison publicly until the closed-deal count is higher.

marketing_spend_pct_revenue.label: Marketing investment as share of revenue
marketing_spend_pct_revenue.hdi_current_note: Requires a revenue figure — not in scope of this dashboard
marketing_spend_pct_revenue.interpretation: Board-level context for whether the conference budget is proportionate. Needs finance input, not marketing data.

linkedin_engagement_rate_pct.label: LinkedIn company page engagement rate
linkedin_engagement_rate_pct.hdi_current_note: Q2 FY2026, from the manual LinkedIn export. Not yet uploaded to the pipeline.
linkedin_engagement_rate_pct.source: LinkedIn page-size cohort ranges, as used in HDI's own Q2 deck
linkedin_engagement_rate_pct.interpretation: The one metric where HDI is clearly outperforming — roughly 4x a company page of its size. Worth leading with, and worth confirming the cohort definition so the multiple holds up to challenge.

_suppression_rules.note: Do not display any rate computed on fewer than 8 records. Show 'not enough data' instead. HDI's per-campaign close rates and win rate both currently sit near or below this threshold.

_for_rob: Six of these have hdi_target: null. Each needs a yes, a number, or an explicit 'use the industry range'.
1. marketing_sourced_pipeline_pct — the only one that reframes the whole project
2. cost_per_lead_usd — requires the lead definition decision first
3. website_visitor_to_lead_pct — pick healthcare or enterprise software band, deliberately
4. linkedin_engagement_rate_pct — already outperforming; setting a target makes it defensible
5. win_rate_by_value_pct — suppress until sample size supports it
6. mql_to_sql_pct — needs an MQL definition before a target means anything
